rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase describes Abu Jahl’s forehead: its owner lies in speech and sins in action.
rows.anchor: أي ناصية أبي جهل كاذبة في قولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A deliberate wrongdoer is punishable, unlike someone who means right but makes a mistake.
rows.anchor: والخاطئ معاقب مأخوذ .   والمخطئ غير مأخوذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing lying and sin to the forehead parallels describing faces as looking in 75:23.
rows.anchor: ووصف الناصية بالكاذبة الخاطئة ،   كوصف الوجوه بالنظر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The wording can describe the owner as liar and sinner, like saying his day fasts and his night stands in prayer.
rows.anchor: أي صاحبها كاذب خاطئ ،   كما يقال : نهاره صائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nādī means the gathering and, by extension, its people and the man’s clan, whom he is challenged to call for help.
rows.anchor: أي أهل مجلسه وعشيرته ،   فليستنصر بهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others identify the zabāniya as stern, powerful angels.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وغيره - واحدهم زبني

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī gives zabnī as the singular form of zabāniya.
rows.anchor: واحدهم زبني .   قاله الكسائي

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash gives zābin as the singular form of zabāniya.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش : زابن .   أبو عبيدة : زبنية

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda gives zabniya as the singular form.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيدة : زبنية .   وقيل : زباني

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another proposed singular is zabānī; another analysis treats the word as a collective plural like abābīl or ʿabādīd.
rows.anchor: وقيل : زباني .   وقيل : هو اسم للجمع ،   كالأبابيل والعباديد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: In Arab usage the zabāniya are the police.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : هم الشرط في كلام العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word derives from zabn, pushing; the sale called muzābana shares this root.
rows.anchor: وهو مأخوذ من الزبن وهو

rows.speaker: أبو الليث السمرقندي
rows.claim: One explanation says they are called zabāniya because they work with their feet as they do with their hands.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنما سموا الزبانية لأنهم يعملون بأرجلهم ،   كما يعملون بأيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abu Jahl boasted he would summon his people after hearing the threat to seize his forelock; hearing of the zabāniya frightened him, and he claimed to have seen a threatening horseman.
rows.anchor: وروي في الخبر أن النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم لما قرأ هذه السورة

rows.speaker: الأخبار
rows.claim: Reports picture the zabāniya with heads in the sky and feet on earth, pushing unbelievers into Hell.
rows.anchor: وفي الأخبار أن الزبانية رؤوسهم في السماء وأرجلهم في الأرض ،   فهم يدفعون الكفار في جهنم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they are the largest angels in creation and the strongest in force.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنهم أعظم الملائكة خلقا ،   وأشدهم بطشا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs also use zabāniya for anyone whose force is formidable.
rows.anchor: والعرب تطلق هذا الاسم على من اشتد بطشه

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet’s description of leaders as zabāniya supports the word’s use for people of formidable strength.
rows.anchor: مطاعيمُ في القُصْوَى مطاعينُ في الوَغَى*** زبانيةٌ غُلْب عِطَامٌ حُلُومُهَا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Via ʿIkrima, Ibn ʿAbbās reports Abu Jahl’s threat to trample the Prophet’s neck and the Prophet’s warning that angels would seize him openly; al-Tirmidhī grades it ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة عن ابن عباس : " سندع الزبانية " قال : قال أبو جهل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Via ʿIkrima, Ibn ʿAbbās says Abu Jahl confronted the Prophet at the Maqām, boasted of his large assembly, and the verses were revealed; had he summoned it, the zabāniya would have seized him immediately. Al-Tirmidhī grades it ḥasan gharīb ṣaḥīḥ.
rows.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال : مر أبو جهل على النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, nādī is the meeting place where people gather, with the intended reference here to the people present.
rows.anchor: والنادي في كلام العرب : المجلس الذي ينتدي فيه القوم ،   أي يجتمعون

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: The line using majlis illustrates the meeting-place sense of nādī.
rows.anchor: كما قال جرير : لهم مجلسٌ صُهْبُ السِّبَالِ أذِلَّةٌ

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s maqāmāt and andiya illustrate that these words refer to assemblies.
rows.anchor: وقال زهير : وفيهمْ مقاماتٌ حسان وُجُوههم

rows.speaker: آخر
rows.claim: The cited verse uses al-majlis for an assembly, supporting the meeting-place sense.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر : واستبَّ بعدك يا كُلَيْبُ المجلِسُ

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: The verb nādaytu means to sit with someone, as Zuhayr’s phrase about a man who sits with the tribe shows.
rows.anchor: وقد ناديت الرجل أناديه إذا جالسته

rows.anchor: أي أهل مجلسه وعشيرته ،   فليستنصر بهم

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s maqāmāt and andiya illustrate that these words refer to assemblies.
rows.anchor: وقال زهير : وفيهمْ مقاماتٌ حسان وُجُوههم

rows.speaker: آخر
rows.claim: The cited verse uses al-majlis for an assembly, supporting the meeting-place sense.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر : واستبَّ بعدك يا كُلَيْبُ المجلِسُ

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: The verb nādaytu means to sit with someone, as Zuhayr’s phrase about a man who sits with the tribe shows.
rows.anchor: وقد ناديت الرجل أناديه إذا جالسته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rejects Abu Jahl’s assumption that he can prevent the Prophet through his power.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : " كلا " أي ليس الأمر على ما يظنه أبو جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must not obey Abu Jahl’s demand that he stop praying.
rows.anchor: " لا تطعه " أي فيما دعاك إليه من ترك الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to prostrate means to pray to God.
rows.anchor: " واسجد " أي صل لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Approach God through obedience and worship.
rows.anchor: " واقترب " أي تقرب إلى اللّه جل ثناؤه بالطاعة والعبادة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says to draw near to God through supplication while prostrating.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المعنى : إذا سجدت فاقترب من الله بالدعاء

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports from Abū Hurayra that the servant is nearest and most beloved to his Lord when prostrating with his forehead on the ground.
rows.anchor: أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه ،   وأحبه إليه ،   جبهته في الأرض

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: Prostration is the utmost servitude and humility; since God has absolute majesty, the worshipper’s abasement brings nearness to Paradise and His abode.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا : وإنما كان ذلك لأنها نهاية العبودية والذلة ،   ولله غاية العزة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A ṣaḥīḥ hadith says to glorify God in bowing and strive in supplication during prostration, where prayers are likely to be answered.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح : أن النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم قال : [ أما الركوع فعظموا فيه الرب

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poem expresses the paradox that humble submission before God is itself a source of honor.
rows.anchor: وإذا تذللت الرقاب تواضعًا *** منا إليك فعِزُّهَا في ذُلِّهَا

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd b. Aslam reads the command as telling Muhammad to pray while Abu Jahl approaches the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم : اسجد أنت يا محمد مصليا ،   واقترب أنت يا أبا جهل من النار

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says the apparent sense is the prostration of prayer, given the passage’s context about prayer.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي : " والظاهر أنه سجود الصلاة " لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ṣaḥīḥ report from Abū Hurayra explicitly says he prostrated with the Prophet in al-Inshiqāq and Iqraʾ, establishing this as a recitation prostration.
rows.anchor: من رواية مسلم وغيره من الأئمة عن أبي هريرة أنه قال : سجدت مع رسول الله

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A report from ʿAlī lists four decisive prostrations: alif-lām-mīm, Ḥā-mīm Tanzīl, al-Najm, and Iqraʾ.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه ،   قال : عزائم السجود أربع : " ألم " و " حم تنزيل

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says that if ʿAlī’s report is authentic, it would also require the second prostration in al-Ḥajj despite its association with bowing.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن العربي : وهذا إن صح يلزم عليه السجود الثاني من سورة " الحج "

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Nāfiʿ and Muṭarrif report that Mālik would privately prostrate at the end of this sūra.
rows.anchor: وقد قال ابن نافع ومطرف : وكان مالك يسجد في خاصة نفسه بخاتمة هذه السورة

rows.speaker: ابن وهب
rows.claim: Ibn Wahb considered the final prostration of the sūra one of the decisive prostrations.
rows.anchor: وابن وهب يراها من العزائم

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: A report through Mālik, Rabīʿa, and Nāfiʿ says that when Iqraʾ was revealed, Muʿādh was told to write it; the tablet, pen, and inkwell prostrated and prayed for the revelation’s blessing, then Muʿādh and the Prophet prostrated.
rows.anchor: وقد روينا من حديث مالك بن أنس عن ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال : لما أنزل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the answer to the oath: people are disposed to be ungrateful for blessings.
rows.anchor: هذا جواب لنعم القسم ،   أي طبع الإنسان على كفران النعمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines kanūd as very ungrateful and denying God’s blessings.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : " لكنود " لكفور جحود لنعم الله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the kanūd recalls calamities and forgets blessings; a poet restates this contrast.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قال الحسن .   وقال : يذكر المصائب ،   وينسى النعم

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poem illustrates ingratitude as complaining of calamities while forgetting blessings.
rows.anchor: إلى متى أنت وحَتَّى مَتَى *** تشكو المصيباتِ وتنسى النعم

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي
rows.claim: The Prophet defines the kanūd as one who eats alone, withholds his gifts, and beats his servant; al-Tirmidhī al-Ḥakīm transmits it in Nawādir al-Uṣūl without a grading stated here.
rows.anchor: الكنود ،   هو الذي يأكل وحده ،   ويمنع رفده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another Prophetic report calls the worst person one who lives alone, withholds his gift, and lashes his servant; al-Tirmidhī al-Ḥakīm transmits it in Nawādir al-Uṣūl.
rows.anchor: من نزل وحده ،   ومنع رفده ،   وجلد عبده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says kanūd means disobedient in Kinda and Ḥaḍramawt dialects.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن عباس أيضا أنه قال : الكنود بلسان كندة وحضر موت : العاصي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the dialects of Rabīʿa and Muḍar, Ibn ʿAbbās says kanūd means unbelieving or ungrateful.
rows.anchor: وبلسان ربيعة ومضر : الكفور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
rows.claim: In the Kināna dialect kanūd means miserly and bad in one’s treatment of dependents; Muqātil gives this view too.
rows.anchor: وبلسان كنانة : البخيل السيء الملكة ،   وقاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poetic usage glosses kanūd as ungrateful toward people’s favors.
rows.anchor: كنودٌ لنعماءِ الرجال ومن يكن *** كَنُودًا لنعماءِ الرجال يُبَعَّدِ

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says the kanūd rejects small favors and fails to thank for much.
rows.anchor: ثم قيل : هو الذي يكفر باليسير ،   ولا يشكر الكثير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view defines kanūd as one who denies the truth.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الجاحد للحق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A wordplay says the tribe Kinda was named so because it denied its father.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنما سميت كندة كندة ؛ لأنها جحدت أباها

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن هرمة
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm b. Hirma’s verse uses kanūd for a miserly woman whose stinginess is remembered.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم بن هرمة الشاعر : دعِ البُخَلاَءَ إن شمخُوا وصَدُّوا*** وذكرَى بُخْلٍ غانيةٍ كَنودِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another etymology derives kanūd from cutting: the ungrateful person cuts off the thanks that should be maintained; kand al-ḥabl means to cut a rope.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الكنود من كند إذا قطع ،   كأنه يقطع ما ينبغي أن يواصله من الشكر

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line uses kannādah in a context of cutting, evidence for the root’s sense of severing.
rows.anchor: تُمِيطِي بصُلْبِ الفؤاد *** وَصُولِ حبالٍ وكَنَّادَهَا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kand yaknud means to deny a blessing; kanūd is the masculine form, and kanūd or kand can also describe a woman.
rows.anchor: فهو كنود .   وامرأة كنود أيضا ،   وكند مثله

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s verse calls a woman kanūd toward the regular visitor’s affection, ungrateful for continued connection.
rows.anchor: أَحْدِثْ لها تُحْدِثْ لوصلكَ إنَّهَا *** كُنُدٌ لوصل الزائر المعتاد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes “the human” here to mean the unbeliever and compares him to barren ground that grows nothing.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : الإنسان هنا الكافر ،   يقول : إنه لكفور

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the verse was revealed about al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines kanūd as one who withholds what is due and cites a poem about being kanūd toward a visitor’s affection.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد : الكنود : المانع

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الواسطي
rows.claim: Abū Bakr al-Wāsiṭī defines the kanūd as one who spends God’s blessings in disobedience to God.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الواسطي : الكنود : الذي ينفق نعم الله

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Abū Bakr al-Warrāq says the kanūd attributes blessings to himself and his helpers.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق : الكنود : الذي يرى النعمة من نفسه

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī defines the kanūd as one who sees the blessing but not the Benefactor.
rows.anchor: وقال الترمذي : الذي يرى النعمة ،   ولا يرى المنعم

rows.speaker: ذو النون المصري
rows.claim: Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī says both the halūʿ and kanūd see the blessing but not its giver.
rows.anchor: وقال ذو النون المصري : الهلوع والكنود : هو الذي يرى النعمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation calls the kanūd resentful and envious.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو الحقود الحسود

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view calls him ignorant of his own worth; a maxim says that one who fails to know his worth exposes his veil.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو الجهول لقدره .   وفي الحكمة : من جهل قدره هتك ستره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All the views return to ingratitude and denial; if sound, the Prophet’s interpretation through blameworthy traits is the highest and settles the matter.
rows.anchor: قلت : هذه الأقوال كلها ترجع إلى معنى الكفران والجحود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “indeed he” refers to the human, with no disagreement reported.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : " وإنه " أي الإنسان من غير خلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khayr means wealth, as in the Qurʾānic phrase about leaving wealth in a will.
rows.anchor: لحب الخير } أي المال ،   ومنه قوله تعالى : { إن ترك خيرا }

rows.speaker: عدي
rows.claim: ʿAdī’s poem uses al-khayr in the context of what souls seek, paired with love of life.
rows.anchor: ماذا تُرَجِّي النفوسُ من طلب ال***خَيْرِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shadīd means powerful in his love of wealth.
rows.anchor: " لشديد " أي لقوي في حبه للمال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes shadīd to mean miserly; a miser is called shadīd or mutashaddid, as in Ṭarafa’s verse about a miserly owner of choice wealth.
rows.anchor: وقيل : " لشديد " لبخيل .   ويقال للبخيل : شديد ومتشدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fāḥisha can mean miserliness, as in 2:268.
rows.anchor: والفاحش : البخيل أيضا .   ومنه قوله تعالى : { ويأمركم بالفحشاء }

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says God calls wealth good because people regard it as good although it may be evil and unlawful; similarly, people call jihad harmful in 3:174.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد : سمى الله المال خيرا ،   وعسى أن يكون شرا وحراما

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains an order shift from “strong in love of wealth”: love is omitted at the end because it was just mentioned and for the verse ending, like “a stormy day” with wind understood in 14:18.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : نظم الآية أن يقال : وإنه لشديد الحب للخير ،   فلما تقدم الحب قال : شديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is Meccan according to the author; Qatāda and a report from Ibn ʿAbbās place it in Medina. It has three verses.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية .   وقال قتادة : مدنية ،   وروي عن ابن عباس ،   وهي ثلاث آيات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Al-ʿaṣr means time or an age, like al-dahr; a poem equates a day of passion with a month and its month with an age.
rows.anchor: أي الدهر ،   قاله ابن عباس وغيره .   فالعصر مثل الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by time because changing circumstances and their succession point to the Creator.
rows.anchor: لما فيه من التنبيه بتصرف الأحوال وتبدلها ،   وما فيها من الدلالة على الصانع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes al-ʿaṣr as night and day, called the two ʿaṣrs in Ḥumayd b. Thawr’s poem.
rows.anchor: وقيل : العصر : الليل والنهار .   قال حميد بن ثور : ولن يلبث العصران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿaṣrān can also mean morning and evening, as in a poem about delaying someone from morning until evening.
rows.anchor: والعصران أيضا : الغداة والعشي .   قال : وأمطله العصرين حتى يملني

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-ʿaṣr can mean the afternoon, from the sun’s zenith until sunset; a poem says the afternoon has grown short.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه العشي ،   وهو ما بين زوال الشمس وغروبها .   قاله الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda also identifies al-ʿaṣr as the final hour of daylight.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة أيضا : هو آخر ساعة من ساعات النهار

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says the oath is by the ʿAṣr prayer, the middle prayer because it is best; a ṣaḥīḥ report identifies the middle prayer as ʿAṣr.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو قسم بصلاة العصر ،   وهي الوسطى ؛ لأنها أفضل الصلوات ،   قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A ṣaḥīḥ hadith says the middle prayer is the ʿAṣr prayer.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر الصحيح " الصلاة الوسطى صلاة العصر "

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the oath concerns the Prophet’s era, distinguished by the renewal of prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو قسم بعصر النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم ،   لفضله بتجديد النبوة فيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The oath can be understood elliptically as “by the Lord of the age.”
rows.anchor: وقيل : معناه ورب العصر

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik rules that one who swears not to speak to someone for an ʿaṣr must avoid speaking for a year.
rows.anchor: قال مالك : من حلف ألا يكلم رجلا عصرا لم يكلمه سنة

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī explains that Mālik chose a year as the broadest reported meaning, following his strict approach to oaths.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي : إنما حمل مالك يمين الحالف ألا يكلم امرأ عصرا على السنة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says the oath is fulfilled after an hour unless the swearer intended another duration.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي : يبر بساعة ،   إلا أن تكون له نية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurṭubī agrees with al-Shāfiʿī; if the swearer is Arab, ask what he intended and accept a plausible interpretation except the shortest one.
rows.anchor: وبه أقول ،   إلا أن يكون الحالف عربيا ،   فيقال له : ما أردت ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse is the answer to the oath.
rows.anchor: هذا جواب القسم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report through Abū Ṣāliḥ, Ibn ʿAbbās says “the human” means the unbeliever.
rows.anchor: والمراد به الكافر ،   قاله ابن عباس في رواية أبي صالح

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk transmits that the verse targets a group of polytheists, including al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra and al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil.
rows.anchor: وروى الضحاك عنه قال : يريد جماعة من المشركين : الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes al-insān to mean humankind as a whole; verse 3’s exception confirms this as the sound reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يعني بالإنسان جنس الناس .   { لفي خسر } لفي غبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khusr means loss; al-Akhfash glosses it as destruction, al-Farrāʾ as punishment, Ibn Zayd as evil, and another view as deficiency, all close in meaning.
rows.anchor: لفي غبن .   وقال الأخفش : هلكة .   الفراء : عقوبة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses khusr as evil; another view calls it deficiency.
rows.anchor: ابن زيد : لفي شر .   وقيل : لفي نقص .   المعنى متقارب

rows.speaker: سلام
rows.claim: Salām reads al-ʿaṣr with kasra on the ṣād.
rows.anchor: وروي عن سلام { والعصر } بكسر الصاد

rows.speaker: الأعرج وطلحة وعيسى الثقفي
rows.claim: Al-Aʿraj, Ṭalḥa, and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read khusr with ḍamma on sīn; Hārūn transmits it from Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, with vowel-following as the basis for the variants.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج وطلحة وعيسى الثقفي " خسر " بضم السين

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A recitation attributed to ʿAlī adds “vicissitudes of time” and further words; Qurṭubī says this is not recited Qurʾān and the received muṣḥaf text is correct.
rows.anchor: وكان علي يقرؤها ( والعصر ونوائب الدهر ،   إن الإنسان لفي خسر

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm says aging and weakness bring decline except for believers whose youthful deeds continue to be credited, comparing it to 95:4–5; he transmits expanded wording that Qurṭubī rejects as Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم : إن الإنسان إذا عمر في الدنيا وهرم ،   لفي نقص وضعف تراجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound text is the reading followed by the community and muṣḥafs; wording that opposes the ʿUthmānic codex is not Qurʾān to recite.
rows.anchor: والصحيح ما عليه الأمة والمصاحف .   وقد مضى الرد في مقدمة الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is from al-insān, which here means people as a whole; this is the sound interpretation.
rows.anchor: استثناء من الإنسان ؛   إذ هو بمعنى الناس على الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing righteous deeds means carrying out the prescribed obligations; Qurṭubī identifies the believers as the Prophet’s Companions.
rows.anchor: أي أدوا الفرائض المفترضة عليهم ،   وهم أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb asks the Prophet for the sūra’s meaning: the oath is by late day, the human in loss is Abū Jahl, faith is Abū Bakr, righteous deeds ʿUmar, truth ʿUthmān, and patience ʿAlī; Ibn ʿAbbās also preached this as a Companion report.
rows.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب : قرأت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم { والعصر } ما تفسيرها يا نبي الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawāṣaw means loving one another, advising one another, and urging one another on.
rows.anchor: { وتواصوا } أي تحابوا

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that al-ḥaqq means declaring God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: { بالحق } أي بالتوحيد ،   كذا روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says al-ḥaqq means the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : { بالحق } أي القرآن

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says al-ḥaqq here is God Himself.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي : الحق هنا هو الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual exhortation to patience means patience in obeying God and refraining from disobedience.
rows.anchor: على طاعة الله عز وجل ،   والصبر عن معاصيه

rows.speaker: عطاء وجابر وابن عباس
rows.claim: The sūra has seven verses; ʿAṭāʾ, Jābir, and one report from Ibn ʿAbbās call it Meccan, while another report from Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and others call it Medinan.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية ،   في قول عطاء وجابر وأحد قولي ابن عباس .   ومدنية ،   في قول له آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dīn means requital and accounting in the Hereafter, as discussed in al-Fātiḥa.
rows.anchor: أي بالجزاء والحساب في الآخرة ،   وقد تقدم في " الفاتحة "

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the retained second hamza: the verb does not occur as rayta, and the interrogative alif eases the hamza to an alif.
rows.anchor: ذكره الزجاج .   وفي الكلام حذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speech has an omitted clause: “Have you seen the one who denies the Judgment—is he right or mistaken?”
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف ،   والمعنى : أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين : أمصيب هو أم مخطئ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that it was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil; al-Kalbī and Muqātil give the same identification.
rows.anchor: فذكر أبو صالح عن ابن عباس قال : نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي ،   وقاله الكلبي ومقاتل

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that it was revealed about an unnamed hypocrite.
rows.anchor: وروى الضحاك عنه قال : نزلت في رجل من المنافقين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says it was revealed about al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the person as Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: وقيل : في أبي جهل

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk also identifies the person as ʿAmr b. ʿĀʾidh.
rows.anchor: الضحاك : في عمرو بن عائذ

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it was revealed about Abū Sufyān, who slaughtered a camel weekly and struck away an orphan who asked him for something.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج : نزلت في أبي سفيان ،   وكان ينحر في كل أسبوع جزورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaduʿʿ means to push away, as in 52:13, where people are driven toward Hell.
rows.anchor: و " يدع " أي يدفع ،   كما قال : { يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا }

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that he pushes the orphan away from his right.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك عن ابن عباس : { فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم } أي يدفعه عن حقه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the person oppresses and wrongs the orphan; the meanings are close.
rows.anchor: قتادة : يقهره ويظلمه .   والمعنى متقارب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As discussed in al-Nisāʾ, people denied women and children inheritance, claiming only those who fight with spear and sword should control wealth.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في سورة " النساء " {[16465]} أنهم كانوا لا يورثون النساء ولا الصغار

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says whoever shelters a Muslim orphan until the orphan is self-sufficient is guaranteed Paradise; no grading is stated here.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم أنه قال : " من ضم يتيما من المسلمين حتى يستغني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl means punishment; Qurṭubī notes that this has been explained in several earlier passages.
rows.anchor: أي عذاب لهم .   وقد تقدم في غير موضع
